correctness.rationale: In the intrinsic rank hyperplane, projected coordinate normal norms equal q=sqrt((n-1)/n) and split normal p=sqrt(hs/n). Eroding true facets gives bounds t=qR<=ci<=1−t and sum_first_h ci<=r−pR. Summation yields necessary R<=R0=min(k,n−k)/(nq), R<=RL=r/(hq+p), R<=RU=(s−k+r)/(sq+p). For any R below all, the first block sum interval [max(ht,k−s(1−t)),min(h(1−t),k−st,r−pR)] is nonempty; block-uniform coordinates construct feasible centers. Equality determines uniform/two cubical phases/unique ties; a cube slice of level alpha has C(m,alpha) binary vertices when integral or m*C(m−1,floor alpha) when not. Independent unrestricted scipy LP at five admissible parameter points, including n=9 lower/upper examples and n=8 equal branch, returned analytic R to 1e−8. The all-parameter proof is analytic, not inferred from those LPs.

value.rationale: The both-sided elementary split matroid is a canonical, naturally parameterized hypersimplex truncation. Complete Chebyshev radius, all-center geometry and exact contact/vertex strata supply useful metric classification beyond the previously studied capacity-one panhandle special case. Strict cubical phases are high-dimensional and not trivial one-vertex examples.

limitations: Only single split and genuinely interior r,u, not arbitrary split-matroid intersections; an earlier general Chebyshev-center result remains possible.
